message.reasoning:
I am ready to play Monopoly and make a decision.

I have $1618 and am on VENTNOR_AVENUE. I control two monopolies with houses and several unmortgaged properties. The opponent has only $20 and heavily mortgaged assets. I must choose an action now.

I will build houses on St Charles Place and States Avenue to complete the pink monopoly. The opponent cannot afford to buy houses, so I will keep the bank short on housing.

I considered hoteling Virginia Avenue to complete the pink monopoly. That would return four houses to the bank, but the even-building rule allows one house difference between properties in a group.

Hotel would return four houses to the bank, which the opponent could later buy. I will keep the remaining three houses on my pink properties instead. The opponent must survive several turns and collect rent or GO money before they can afford any houses.

I checked the rent values for the opponent's red properties. Even with one house, Kentucky and Indiana would only raise rent to $250, while Illinois would reach $300. That is a modest increase, so keeping the bank short on houses is a solid defensive move.

Unmortgaging the yellow properties would cost over four hundred dollars. That is too expensive while the opponent still controls reds. I will keep my cash buffer intact and avoid building a third monopoly.

Hoteling is possible because the four houses already on the property return to the bank. That would flood the bank with houses and leave the opponent with too much cash to build.

I will not trade Park Place. That would complete the opponent's dark blue monopoly, and they would need to unmortgage everything to use it.

If the opponent lands on my orange properties with four houses, they will owe $750 to $800. They may sell houses to pay that rent. That returns houses to the bank and reduces their threat. I can then buy those houses back on my next turn.

I cannot buy returned houses in the same action, so they would remain available to the opponent. Hoteling is only viable if the opponent is broke and cannot build. The real danger to me is the opponent landing on my orange properties with four houses, not the threat from their reds.

I will build one house on St Charles Place and one on States Avenue. The opponent cannot afford to buy the returned houses, so I will leave one house in the bank. I will end the turn after this action.
